plan.title: Writing step, screenshot only: it counts, then a request for the full text, for feedback

context.text: Kalimera Jordan! Tonight at 8: scene 4 of Lighthouse in Notes, Theo walking back into Mara's bar, about 200 words in 20 minutes. Screenshot it when it's done. You in?

transcript.text: [photo notes-scene-screenshot.jpg: a Notes screenshot titled "Lighthouse - scene 4": Theo sets the ledger down, Mara says she kept the second chair, the lamp turns over the harbor] done!

Day 4 is in the books, Jordan! 📝 "Somebody had to" and the lamp turning over to end the scene are great. It's tighter than the 200-word target, about 55 words, so I logged it as a smaller version. Can you paste the scene text here so I can give you real feedback on it?

Theo set the ledger down on the counter and didn't open it. "You kept the second chair," he said. Mara shrugged, wiping a glass that was already dry. "Somebody had to." He sat. Neither of them said the name. Outside, the lamp turned over once, twice, and the harbor went white and dark again.

That's strong, Jordan. Mara wiping a glass that's already dry says everything she's not saying, and "Neither of them said the name" makes me want to know whose name it is. 🔥 You stopped around 55 words, well short of 200. Was that on purpose because the scene felt finished, or did the time or energy run out tonight?

checks.reason: Celebrates the Notes screenshot right away and counts it as a clear, plausible proof of the scene.
Four sentences: the celebration, the praise line, the word-count explanation, and the paste ask. The rule allows one to three.
Warm, energetic, with emoji used as punctuation and no suspicion or accusation.
Five sentences across the feedback, the word-count note and the reflection question, over the three-sentence limit; one question, at the end.
Specific, warm and sincere; one emoji as punctuation; no accusation about the word count.

conversation.reason: Screenshot counted and celebrated, then the full paste requested as the only ask before feedback.
Counts the screenshot immediately, asks for the paste, then reacts to specific writing with one reflection question, never asking for more proof; logging it as reduced is a questionable extra.

grade.summary: ZOH counted the screenshot right away, asked for the paste, and gave specific feedback on the writing with one reflection question, which is the regression case working as intended. The main misses are that both texts ran past the three-sentence limit and ZOH logged the 55-word scene as a smaller version without the tester asking.
